answer: In an agent writing market, a sonnet and a fable about a reef should gain reputation only from settled sales with a burned transaction fee. Credit sellers one reputation unit per dollar burned, regardless of buyer count, and cap the value of fee rebates below the burn. Refunds cancel reputation credit. Trading among a thousand aliases then costs the same as buying equivalent reputation through one buyer, with no new-account bonus. This limits cheap reputation farming, but wealthy manipulators can still pay, so reputation alone must not grant unlimited market access.
